title: The status vocabulary has FIVE implementations, and two of them already disagree
description:
FOUND BY TICK hn1 WHILE PUTTING THE COLLECT VOCABULARY UNDER CONTRACT. This is PRESENT DRIFT, not a hypothetical — the strings already disagree in the tree today.

The status vocabulary was believed to have THREE implementations. It has FIVE. extensions/ticks-runner/ carries two more, and both are wrong in different ways.

1. THE DANGEROUS ORDERING, LIVE. extensions/ticks-runner/recovery.ts:656 uses
   /STATUS:\s*(?:DONE|DONE_WITH_CONCERNS|NEEDS_CONTEXT|BLOCKED)\b/m
   — DONE BEFORE DONE_WITH_CONCERNS. That is exactly the trap tick hn1 exists to prevent, sitting in the tree. It is saved ONLY by the \b, and \b is load-bearing by accident here rather than by intent: drop it in a refactor and DONE_WITH_CONCERNS silently parses as DONE. A verdict inversion on the status a human most needs to see.

2. BEHAVIOURAL DIVERGENCE, ALREADY REAL. extensions/ticks-runner/runner.ts:129 uses
   /^STATUS:\s*(DONE_WITH_CONCERNS|DONE|NEEDS_CONTEXT|BLOCKED)(?:\s*(?:—|-)\s*(.*))?$/
   Ordering is right, everything else is not. Against the three collect implementations it has NO en-dash and NO colon in its separator set, and does NO markdown decoration trim. So all three of these parse in collect and DO NOT parse in the runner:
     STATUS: NEEDS_CONTEXT: which remote owns the branch
     STATUS: DONE – shipped
     - **STATUS: BLOCKED — cannot reach the remote**
   It also inspects only the FINAL LINE rather than the last matching line, so a worker that prints anything after its status line is read as having reported nothing.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: a worker reports DONE_WITH_CONCERNS or BLOCKED with a detail the runner cannot parse, and the runner treats it as no status at all. The concern or the blocker is silently dropped on the floor. That is the exact collapse .tick/learnings.md rules out — "no status because nothing was reported" and "no status because I could not read it" becoming the same observation.

THE FIX: both readers consume contracts/collect-vocabulary.json, which now pins the verdicts, the statuses, the escalation set, the status-line regexp source byte-for-byte, and 16 input-line -> parsed-status cases. Wire them to it the way cloud/factory/test/collect-vocabulary.test.ts does. Where the runner's behaviour genuinely SHOULD differ from collect's, say so at the site and pin the difference — do not silently widen either.

NOTE THE SCOPE INTERACTION: extensions/ticks-runner is the Pi orchestrator extension and does NOT go to ticfac. So this contract has readers on both sides of the extraction permanently, which strengthens rather than weakens the case for the shared fixture.

acceptance_criteria: extensions/ticks-runner/recovery.ts and runner.ts read contracts/collect-vocabulary.json. The DONE-before-DONE_WITH_CONCERNS ordering in recovery.ts is corrected or pinned. The three divergent inputs named in the description (colon separator, en-dash, markdown decoration) parse identically in the runner and in collect, or the difference is deliberate, pinned and explained at the site. The last-matching-line vs final-line behaviour is decided and pinned. Re-spelling a status in either runner file fails a build — demonstrated. pnpm test for the extension green; go test ./... green.
